text: Status: numerically verified correct. P0/P1 issues msdt.R. Verification run (sourced R/msdt.R, lineup size 6): - CDF identity pmax_filler(q) == pnorm(q)^(m-1) ✓ - Quantile round-trip pmax_filler(qmax_filler(p)) == p ✓ - lower.tail=FALSE consistent 1-p ✓ - max_filler_moments(6)$mean = 1.162964 matches known E[max 5 N(0,1)] = 1.16296; Monte-Carlo mean 1.1613; var 0.4475, skewness +0.303 (correct sign/scale) ✓ - Parameter recovery exact: γ=0.5, d′=1.2 → recovered γ=0.5, d′=1.2 ✓ - rmax_filler sample mean 1.1622 vs theory 1.1630 ✓ Docs accuracy: vignette msdt_model.Rmd formulas Pr(REJ|)=Φ(γ)^m, Pr(REJ|G)=Φ(γ−d′)Φ(γ)^{m−1} match implementation exactly; scope caveats (equal variance, independent fillers) honestly stated. Reference Yang, Burke & Healy (2025) present. Minor (P2): - pmax_filler(log.p=TRUE) dmax_filler(log=TRUE) can return -Inf extreme lower tail (log(0)); acceptable, guard tidiness. - R/max_sdt_fit.R (compound-decision MAX SDT fitter, commit 023d004) yet reviewed pass — review model-comparison mini-pass.

what: R/max_sdt_fit.R (compound-decision MAX SDT fitter) — reviewed + FIXED
title: r4lineups — CRAN/JOSS Audit Findings
text: FIXED (session). Applied: (1) deterministic multistart grid (finer λ) + Nelder-Mead polish replacing single boundary-prone start; (2) proper partition cells {correct-ID, filler-ID, reject} replacing overlapping {hit, choose} cells; (3) floored expected counts (pmax(pred,1e-8)) replacing pred>0.5 cell-exclusion created plateau; (4) corrected GoF df = 3*n_conditions − np; (5) honest convergence reporting (forced 0L); fix bootstrap helper .max_sdt_make_obj. Verified: documented example now d′=1.94, λ=1.15, χ²(1)=4.41; exact parameter recovery three (d′,λ) pairs; two-condition df 2/3; reproducible bootstrap CIs. Updated two tests test-max-sdt-fit.R asserted old df (3→1, 6→2). 30 tests pass. Original analysis retained record. Model probabilities verified correct: hit_prob = ∫_λ^∞ φ(x−d)Φ(x)^{n−1}dx, tpc_prob = 1−Φ(λ−d)Φ(λ)^{n−1}, fa_prob = 1−Φ(λ)^n. full-information fitter (uses five outcome counts), right tool choice data available. P0 — optimizer returns non-global boundary estimate. documented headline example (n_hit=69,n_tp_choose=82,n_fa=64,N_tp=96,N_ta=106) returns d′=1.85, λ=−5 (pinned lower bound), χ²=18.68, predicting everyone chooses (reject cells→0). Profiling objective shows much better fit λ≈1.0, d′≈3.2, χ²≈8.3; proper-partition objective minimises λ≈1.1, d′≈1.9, χ²≈4.6 (pass GoF). Root causes: (1) flat plateau low λ reject predictions ≈0 dropped pred > 0.5 cell filter; (2) χ² spike λ=0; (3) single start (1,0) + boundary-prone L-BFGS-B, multistart. Net effect: reported d′ can badly wrong. Fix: add multistart λ grid (e.g. −2..2) /robust objective; reconsider pred>0.5 exclusion flattens surface; widen/relax bounds penalise boundary. P1 — GoF degrees freedom overstated. df = n_cells − n_params = 5 − 2 = 3 (one condition) ignores two fixed row totals (choose+reject=N_tp, fa+reject=N_ta). Correct df = (3-cat TP → 2) + (2-cat TA → 1) − 2 params = 1. Two-condition case: code gives 10−4=6, correct 2. p-values lenient. (compare_max_sdt Δdf correct.) P2 — overlapping cells + convergence masking. χ² objective uses {n_hit, n_tp_choose} n_hit ⊂ n_tp_choose (double-counts choosers); cleaner partition {correct-ID, filler-ID, reject}. bootstrap simulator (L346-348) nest hits correctly, objective bootstrap DGP inconsistent. Also opt$convergence <- 0L forced Nelder-Mead fallback (max_sdt_fit.R:284) masks non-convergence — pattern flagged Winter 2-HT. P1 — documented example poor showcase: produces boundary/degenerate fit . Replace data yield interior, well-fitting solution optimizer fixed. Documentation gap (P1, code bug): - estimate_msdt_params() method--moments estimator exactly identified two rejection rates (Pr(REJ|) fixes γ; CA→CP rejection gap fixes d′). information-lossy — ignores choice composition (suspect-ID vs filler-ID) filler-choice spread, diagnostic outcomes (cf. Sporer choosers vs non-choosers). .Rd vignette state explicitly point users full response breakdowns likelihood-based fitter (max_sdt_fit.R) / 2-HT model. Frame JOSS paper way reviewer doesn’t read rejection-estimation recommended mSDT fit.

title: r4lineups — CRAN/JOSS Audit Findings
text: Method verified benchmarks (make_fullroc_data ): - Identical TP/TA response distributions → AUC = 0.527 (≈0.5; curve ends exactly (1,1)) ✓ — see bias note . - Perfect separation (TP→suspect, TA→reject) → AUC = 1.000 ✓ - Realistic (TP suspect-heavy) → AUC 0.78 (diagnosticity) / 0.77 (apriori) ✓ Construction correct: responses crossed confidence, category gets HR=n/n_tp FAR=n/n_ta, ordered DR (descending) -priori, cumulated span (0,0)→(1,1). Epsilon affects ordering (DR FAR=0), curve coordinates; empty cells dropped; trapezoidal AUC correct. P2 — order="apriori" + conf_bins raises “NAs introduced coercion”. [FIXED] -priori confidence tiebreak .numeric(conf_bin); conf_bins labels "conf_1", … → NA, silently breaking within-decision ordering. Fixed sorting bin index .integer(factor(conf_bin, levels = conf_levels)). Verified: warning, AUC 0.77, order now suspect(hi→lo)→filler(lo→hi)→reject(lo→hi), curve ends (1,1); default ordering unchanged (regression clean). P1 (doc, bug) — diagnosticity ordering optimistically biased. Sorting cells sample DR bows curve upward noise alone: identical TP/TA → AUC 0.527, 0.500; bias grows number (decision×conf) cells, shrinks N. Smith & Yang offer -priori ordering. .Rd/vignette warn diagnosticity-ordered AUC unbiased recommend -priori ordering (permutation baseline) inference. P2 — ggplot2 deprecation plot_fullroc. [PARTLY FIXED] geom_line(size=1) → linewidth fixed. Track B sweep still needed: grep whole package geom_line(size= / geom_*(... size= line-width uses convert linewidth. P1 (CRAN) — \dontrun{} unnecessary. make_fullroc_data/make_fullroc examples use base-R simulated data → make runnable \donttest. Part package-wide cleanup. P2 — defensive idioms. 1:nrow(...) / 2:nrow(...) → seq_len/seq_along.

what: Component 3 — EIG & PPV range (eig_functions.R, ppv_range_functions.R) — reviewed
title: r4lineups — CRAN/JOSS Audit Findings
text: EIG verified correct. EIG = Σ_x p(x)[H(prior) − H(posterior(x))] = mutual information (guilt;response). Checks: uninformative responses → EIG ≈ 0.0007 bits; perfect separation prior 0.5 → EIG = 1.000 bit = H(0.5). Bayes posterior + total-probability weighting correct. P1 — duplicate entropy() definition. [FIXED] Defined twice (internal, exported): eig_functions.R entropy(p, base=2) bayes_curves_functions.R entropy(p). Whichever sourced last collation won package-wide; alphabetical luck (eig bayes) kept working, roxygen merged one entropy.Rd duplicated \usage line. Fixed deleting bayes_curves duplicate; four call sites (2 per file) now resolve single entropy(p, base=2). Verified call styles return 1.0. (Track B: re-run document() clean man/entropy.Rd.) P1 — ppv_by_confidence(correction="effective") computed wrong effective size. [FIXED] -member-data fallback called esize_T(table(pseudo_table)), tabulated values per-position count vector, collapsing E′ near-constant ~1.38 regardless data — “effective” correction silently behaved like “none”. Fixed esize_T(pseudo_table). Verified: E′ now ~5.7 (≈ nominal 6 even lineup), effective PPV (0.879) sits none (0.559) nominal (0.884). (Member-level branch esize_T(table(ta_conf$lineup_member)) already correct.) P2 (doc) — PPV base rate implicit. PPV = n_guilty / (n_guilty + n_innocent_est) mixes raw TP TA counts, prior/base rate implicitly experiment’s TP:TA ratio. base_rate argument exposed. Document , add base-rate parameter, users don’t misread PPV base-rate-free. pseudo-distribution fallback (even filler spread) also modeling approximation worth stating. P1 (CRAN) — \dontrun{} runnable examples: compute_eig, make_eig, ppv_by_confidence, ppv_range_by_confidence examples pure base-R/sim data → make runnable \donttest. Part package-wide cleanup.

title: r4lineups — CRAN/JOSS Audit Findings
text: Math verified correct. C = Σ(n_j/N)(c_j−a_j)², O/U = c̄−ā, NRI = [Σ(n_j/N)(a_j−ā)²]/[ā(1−ā)], ANRI = (N·NRI−J+1)/(N−J+1). Checks: good resolution → NRI 0.234 / ANRI 0.232; flat accuracy → NRI 0 / ANRI −0.0017 (correct small-sample bias correction, can go slightly negative); well-calibrated data → C=0, O/U=0; ANRI formula hand-check exact. Bootstrap CI compare_anri (difference--independent-bootstraps, percentile CI, CI-excludes-0 test) sound. P2 — confidence scale detection silent foot-gun. make_calibration_data infers scale (max(confidence) > 1) divide 100. Likert 1–7 (0–10) scale therefore gets divided 100 → overall_confidence ≈ 0.04, making C O/U meaningless, warning. Verified. Fix options: add explicit confidence_scale = c("auto","0-1","0-100") arg, /warn 1 < max(conf) < ~20 (ambiguous). Touches make_calibration_data callers (compute_anri, make_calibration_by_condition) — handle small coordinated change. P2 — J varies across bootstrap resamples. compute_anri sets J = nrow(non-empty bins); resample empty bin shrinks J, perturbing N−J+1 correction. Minor; consider fixing J = length(confidence_bins) − 1 stability, document. P3 — ANRI can negative (construction, like adjusted R²) — note .Rd. P3 — redundant set.seed(seed) top compare_anri (inner bootstrap_anri calls reseed anyway). \dontrun/example issues (functions ship without @examples; consider adding runnable examples CRAN/JOSS completeness).

what: Component 5 — Bayesian curves & utility (bayes_curves_functions.R, utility_functions.R, dpp_functions.R) — reviewed
title: r4lineups — CRAN/JOSS Audit Findings
text: four sub-parts verified correct; code bugs. - Bayes prior-posterior curves (make_bayes_curves): posterior prior 0.5 matches hand Bayes (0.8257); info_gain = H(prior) − H(posterior) uses now-single entropy(). ✓ - DPP (make_dpp, Smith et al. 2018): DPP = 1 − AUC_obs/AUC_perfect, perfect ROC = rectangle area max_fa. Perfect data → DPP 0; realistic → 0.72. make_rocdata adds (0,0) origin observed/perfect integration domains span [0, max_fa]. ✓ - Expected utility (make_utility_curves, Lampinen et al. 2019): EU decomposition matches hand calc; max-utility criterion selected correctly. ✓ - BREE (make_bree_curve, bayes_curves_functions.R — utility_functions.R earlier inventory said): prior-inversion algebra correct — self-comparison gives delta≡0; cross-comparison yields prior_b whose posterior equals ’s. ✓ P2 (doc/method) — utility FA-rate hybrid. make_utility_curves estimates innocent-suspect FAs n_false_suspects + n_false_fillers/lineup_size. designated innocent suspect double counts (direct innocent-suspect picks + filler-derived estimate); strictly right -designated-suspect designs. modeling issue PPV — document assumption (ideally reconcile two package consistent). P3 (perf) — make_utility_difference/compare_utility recompute make_utility_curves raw data 99 base rates, though per-criterion hit/FA rates don’t depend base rate (EU weighting/argmax ). Compute rates , reweight per base rate. P1 (CRAN) — \dontrun{} compute_dpp, compare_utility (others) — pure sim data, make runnable/\donttest.

title: r4lineups — CRAN/JOSS Audit Findings
text: Model equations verified: TP TA probability vectors sum 1; MPT tree (detect→correct; else biased/guess/reject) matches Winter et al. (2022). Multinomial MLE. Parameter recovery excellent: true (dP,dA,b,g)=(.45,.30,.08,.55) → est (.454,.293,.073,.552). P1 — goodness--fit test summary.winter_2ht statistically invalid (model SATURATED). one TP/TA condition 4 independent data points (2 per 3-cell multinomial given fixed totals) 4 free parameters → 0 residual df. Verified: fitted expected ≡ observed (147→147, 94→94.16, …), χ²≈0.0008. summary() computes df <- 6 - 4 = 2 p-value, always show near-perfect fit (χ²≈0, p≈1) — false reassurance. single-condition 2-HT model tested absolute fit; Winter et al. test via multiple conditions / parameter constraints. Fix: drop single-condition χ² test (replace explicit “saturated, df=0” note; keep observed-vs-expected optimisation sanity check). Paper impact: report 2-HT GoF χ²(2) single-condition fits. Correction prior plan note — convergence masking . plan flagged fit_winter_2ht ~L280-285 forced convergence<-0; misattribution (lines .extract_counts_from_df). fit_winter_2ht reports optim convergence honestly; print/ summary warn non-zero. masking bug max_sdt_fit.R (already fixed). P2 — single start, boundary solutions. One L-BFGS-B start (0.3,0.1,0.05,0.5); example drove dA→0 (boundary), Hessian SEs unreliable. MLE generically unique saturated model, low priority — small multistart + boundary caveat SEs harden . P1 (CRAN) — \dontrun{} fit_winter_2ht example (count-data path pure base R). FIXED (session): summary.winter_2ht now prints “Model identification: Saturated (just-identified), df=0” note plus residual obs-vs-expected discrepancy convergence check, replacing invalid χ²(2) test. Verified.

title: Full ROC Analysis for Eyewitness Lineups (Smith & Yang, 2020)
text: Compute non-cumulative rates decision × confidence category: Order categories DR (diagnosticity) -priori Compute cumulative rates: Calculate AUC using trapezoidal rule:
code: Hit Rate (HR) = P(response | target present) False Alarm Rate (FAR) = P(response | target absent) Diagnosticity Ratio (DR) = HR / FAR Cumulative HR = sum of HRs (ordered by evidence strength) Cumulative FAR = sum of FARs (ordered by evidence strength) AUC = Σ [(FAR_i - FAR_{i-1}) × (HR_i + HR_{i-1})/2]

title: Full ROC Analysis for Eyewitness Lineups (Smith & Yang, 2020)

title: ROC Analysis Comparison Guide: Partial vs. Full
text: Key point: Filler IDs converted estimated suspect IDs dividing lineup size. Rejections completely ignored.
code: For each confidence level (high to low):   HR = P(suspect ID | target present)   FAR = P(suspect ID | target absent) + P(filler ID | target absent) / lineup_size   Plot (FAR, HR) Compute pAUC over limited range

title: ROC Analysis Comparison Guide: Partial vs. Full
text: Key point: responses used directly. Ordering diagnosticity ratio (evidence strength).
code: For each decision × confidence category:   HR = P(response | target present)   FAR = P(response | target absent)   DR = HR / FAR Sort categories by DR (evidence strength) Compute cumulative HR and FAR Plot full ROC curve Compute full AUC over entire [0,1] range

title: ROC Analysis Comparison Guide: Partial vs. Full
text: Consider two procedures: - Conservative: Low suspect ID rate (20%), low false ID rate (5%) - Liberal: High suspect ID rate (40%), high false ID rate (15%) Partial ROC: - Conservative curve: steep slope narrow range [0, 0.05] - Liberal curve: moderate slope wider range [0, 0.15] - Comparing pAUC [0, 0.05]: Conservative wins - : ignores 75% liberal procedure’s suspect IDs! Full ROC: - Conservative curve: steep flat - Liberal curve: moderate throughout - Comparing full AUC [0, 1.0]: Fair comparison - procedures can realize full potential

title: ROC Analysis Comparison Guide: Partial vs. Full
text: pAUC compares conservative’s suspect IDs 1/3 liberal’s suspect IDs. Unfair! Full AUC uses everything. Fair!
code: Conservative Procedure:   Suspect IDs: 20% (TP), 5% (TA)  → pAUC region   Filler IDs:  30% (TP), 40% (TA) → ignored in partial ROC   Rejections:  50% (TP), 55% (TA) → ignored in partial ROC  Liberal Procedure:   Suspect IDs: 40% (TP), 15% (TA) → only 5% used in pAUC comparison!   Filler IDs:  25% (TP), 35% (TA) → ignored   Rejections:  35% (TP), 50% (TA) → ignored

code: data(lineup_example)  set.seed(4) cal_post <- calibration_bayes(   lineup_example,   confidence_bins = c(0, 60, 80, 100),   alpha = 0.5,   S = 1000 )  cal_post #> Bayesian Calibration Analysis - Beta-Binomial model #>   n = 75; 3 confidence bins; prior alpha = 0.50 #>   C (calibration):      mean = 0.0138, median = 0.0107, 95% CI [0.0015, 0.0416] #>   O/U (over/underconf): mean = 0.0351, median = 0.0348, 95% CI [-0.0384, 0.1094] #>   NRI (resolution):     mean = 0.2697, median = 0.2690, 95% CI [0.1344, 0.4067] #>   (Frequentist: C = 0.0081, O/U = 0.0267, NRI = 0.2670) plot(cal_post, metric = "C") plot(cal_post, metric = "NRI")

title: Bayesian Inference for Lineup Measures
text: sdt_compare() compares two conditions using summary SDT counts. draws posterior hit false-alarm rates, converts draw d′d', reports posterior Δd′=dA′−dB′\Delta d' = d'_A - d'_B.
code: set.seed(5) sdt_post <- sdt_compare(   hits_A = 45, misses_A = 55, fas_A = 12, crs_A = 88,   hits_B = 38, misses_B = 62, fas_B = 10, crs_B = 90,   label_A = "Procedure A",   label_B = "Procedure B",   alpha = 0.5,   S = 1000 )  sdt_post #> Bayesian SDT Comparison: Procedure A vs Procedure B #>   Prior: Jeffreys Beta(0.50, 0.50) on HR and FAR #>   Posterior mean d': Procedure A = 1.042, Procedure B = 0.971 #>   Delta d' (Procedure A - Procedure B): #>     Posterior mean:   0.072 #>     Posterior median: 0.072 #>     95% CI: [-0.505, 0.635] #>   P(d'_Procedure A > d'_Procedure B | data): 0.6150 #>   P(d'_Procedure B > d'_Procedure A | data): 0.3850 #>   (Frequentist z-test: z = 0.254, p = 0.7994) plot(sdt_post)

title: Calibration and Decision Analysis
text: vignette demonstrates five advanced statistical methods analyzing eyewitness identification data r4lineups: Calibration Analysis - Assessing confidence-accuracy correspondence Bayesian Information-Gain Curves - Evaluating diagnostic value evidence Expected Utility Analysis - Decision-theoretic evaluation cost/benefit tradeoffs Deviation Perfect Performance (DPP) - ROC-based truncation-robust metric ANRI - Bias-corrected resolution index bootstrap inference methods complement traditional lineup fairness measures providing sophisticated analyses identification accuracy, confidence calibration, decision-making utility.

text: “analyzed identification performance using calibration analysis, DPP, ANRI bootstrap inference. Witnesses showed moderate calibration (C = 0.12, O/U = -0.05), indicating slight overconfidence. DPP 0.34 (95% CI [0.28, 0.41]), indicating performance well chance perfection. Resolution, measured ANRI, 0.25 (95% CI [0.15, 0.36]), demonstrating confidence ratings provided meaningful discrimination correct incorrect identifications. Expected utility analysis revealed confidence threshold 75% maximized utility (EU = 0.42) given base rate 50% specified cost matrix. Bayesian analysis showed high-confidence suspect identifications provided information gain (mean IG = 0.48 bits), substantially reducing uncertainty guilt.”

title: Full ROC Analysis for Eyewitness Lineups
text: vignette demonstrates use full ROC (Receiver Operating Characteristic) curves analyzing eyewitness lineup data, following method developed Smith, Yang, Wells (2020).

title: Full ROC Analysis for Eyewitness Lineups
text: Traditional (partial) ROC analysis lineup data uses suspect identifications, ignoring filler identifications lineup rejections. creates several problems: Incomplete evidence: Filler IDs rejections also provide diagnostic information suspect guilt Biased comparisons: Partial AUC (pAUC) systematically favors conservative procedures Limited range: Partial ROC curves don’t span full [0,1] range Confounded bias: separate discriminability response bias full ROC method addresses issues using eyewitness responses.

title: Full ROC Analysis for Eyewitness Lineups
text: Let’s simulate data two viewing conditions: Expected result: Strong memory condition substantially higher AUC (e.g., 0.85 vs. 0.65).
code: set.seed(123)  # Strong memory (clear viewing) strong_data <- data.frame(   target_present = c(rep(TRUE, 100), rep(FALSE, 100)),   identification = c(     # Target-present: high suspect ID rate     sample(c("suspect", "filler", "reject"), 100, replace = TRUE,            prob = c(0.70, 0.15, 0.15)),     # Target-absent: low false ID rate     sample(c("suspect", "filler", "reject"), 100, replace = TRUE,            prob = c(0.10, 0.30, 0.60))   ),   confidence = sample(seq(0, 100, 10), 200, replace = TRUE) )  # Weak memory (degraded viewing) weak_data <- data.frame(   target_present = c(rep(TRUE, 100), rep(FALSE, 100)),   identification = c(     # Target-present: lower suspect ID rate     sample(c("suspect", "filler", "reject"), 100, replace = TRUE,            prob = c(0.35, 0.35, 0.30)),     # Target-absent: higher false ID rate     sample(c("suspect", "filler", "reject"), 100, replace = TRUE,            prob = c(0.25, 0.40, 0.35))   ),   confidence = sample(seq(0, 100, 10), 200, replace = TRUE) )  # Compute full ROCs strong_roc <- make_fullroc(strong_data) weak_roc <- make_fullroc(weak_data)  # Compare cat("Strong memory AUC:", strong_roc$auc, "\n") cat("Weak memory AUC:", weak_roc$auc, "\n")

text: Instead using every unique confidence value, can create bins:
code: # Create Low (0-60), Medium (60-80), High (80-100) bins result_binned <- make_fullroc(   data,   conf_bins = c(0, 60, 80, 100),   order = "diagnosticity" )  # This creates cleaner ROC curves with fewer operating points # Useful when you have many confidence levels

title: Full ROC Analysis for Eyewitness Lineups
text: Orders response categories empirical diagnosticity ratio (DR = Hit Rate / False Alarm Rate): High DR (e.g., 10.0): Strong evidence guilt (e.g., high-confidence suspect ID) DR ≈ 1.0: Neutral evidence Low DR (e.g., 0.1): Strong evidence innocence (e.g., high-confidence rejection) Caution — optimistic bias. ordering chosen sample diagnosticity ratios, curve bowed upward noise alone: even identical target-present target-absent response distributions produce AUC slightly 0.5. bias grows number decision × confidence cells shrinks sample size. Diagnosticity ordering useful exploration, inference comparisons across conditions prefer -priori ordering () benchmark permutation baseline.
code: result <- make_fullroc(data, order = "diagnosticity")

title: Full ROC Analysis for Eyewitness Lineups
text: Uses theoretical ordering: Order (evidence guilt → evidence innocence): 1. Suspect IDs: high confidence → low confidence 2. Filler IDs: low confidence → high confidence 3. Rejections: low confidence → high confidence Rationale: - High-confidence suspect IDs strong evidence guilt - Low-confidence filler IDs/rejections strong evidence innocence (rare guilty, common innocent) ordering fixed advance rather estimated data, -priori ordering suffer optimistic bias described safer choice hypothesis tests -condition comparisons (Smith & Yang, 2020, offer ).

title: Comparing Models for Eyewitness Identification Data
text: Eyewitness identification data can analyzed using multiple theoretical frameworks, providing unique insights. vignette demonstrates use r4lineups’ model comparison framework fit compare: 2-HT Model (Winter et al., 2022): Multinomial Processing Tree model EIG (Starns et al., 2023): Expected Information Gain Full ROC (Smith & Yang, 2020): Receiver Operating Characteristic compare_models() function provides unified interface fitting models generating comparison tables visualizations.

title: Comparing Models for Eyewitness Identification Data
text: Two-High Threshold (2-HT) model multinomial processing tree (MPT) separates identification decisions distinct latent processes: Parameters: - dP: Detection culprit presence (0-1) - dA: Detection culprit absence (0-1) - b: Biased suspect selection (0-1) - g: Guessing-based selection (0-1) Model equations (target-present): - P(suspect ID) = dP + (1-dP) × [b + (1-b) × g × (1/L)] - P(filler ID) = (1-dP) × (1-b) × g × ((L-1)/L) - P(reject) = (1-dP) × (1-b) × (1-g) Use : - want understand underlying cognitive mechanisms - Testing theories detection vs. guessing - Comparing conditions different bias levels

title: Comparing Models for Eyewitness Identification Data
text: Expected Information Gain quantifies much information witness responses provide guilt vs. innocence using Shannon entropy: Formula: EIG = Σ p(x) × [H(prior) - H(p(guilty|x))] x = response category (e.g., “suspect_high_confidence”) Interpretation: - EIG = 0: information (responses don’t distinguish guilty/innocent) - EIG = 1: Perfect information (complete resolution uncertainty) - Higher EIG = diagnostic procedure Use : - Evaluating overall diagnosticity procedures - Comparing different identification methods - Assessing policy-relevant cutoffs

title: Comparing Models for Eyewitness Identification Data
text: Full ROC uses witness responses (suspect IDs, filler IDs, rejections) compute threshold-free measure discriminability: Measure: - AUC (Area Curve) - Range: 0.5 (chance) 1.0 (perfect) Use : - Measuring investigator discriminability - Comparing system variables (lineup procedures) - Need threshold-free performance measure

title: Statistical Comparison of ROC Curves (pAUC Analysis)
text: evaluating eyewitness identification procedures, often need statistically compare ROC curves conditions. example: simultaneous lineups provide better discriminability sequential lineups? increasing lineup size improve impair performance? different retention intervals affect discriminability? vignette demonstrates use r4lineups’ compare_pauc() function rigorously test differences partial Area Curve (pAUC) conditions using bootstrap-based standard errors z-tests.

title: Statistical Comparison of ROC Curves (pAUC Analysis)
text: comparison uses following statistical framework: Test statistic: Z=pAUC1−pAUC2SE(pAUC1−pAUC2)Z = \frac{pAUC_1 - pAUC_2}{SE(pAUC_1 - pAUC_2)} Standard errors: - Computed via bootstrap resampling (non-parametric) - Typically 1000-2000 bootstrap samples P-value: - Two-tailed test standard normal distribution - Null hypothesis: pAUC₁ = pAUC₂ Confidence interval: CI=(pAUC1−pAUC2)±Zα/2×SE(difference)CI = (pAUC_1 - pAUC_2) \pm Z_{α/2} \times SE(difference)

title: Statistical Comparison of ROC Curves (pAUC Analysis)
text: Partial AUC (pAUC) preferred full AUC several reasons: Policy relevance: Focus acceptable false ID rates (e.g., ≤20%) Practical constraints: Avoid unrealistic operating points Precision: stable estimates relevant region Comparison: Ensures fair comparison false ID rates

# Simulate various sample sizes sample_sizes <- c(50, 100, 150, 200, 300) power_results <- data.frame(   n = sample_sizes,   power = numeric(length(sample_sizes)) )  # For each sample size, run multiple comparisons for (i in seq_along(sample_sizes)) {   n <- sample_sizes[i]    # Run 50 simulations (use 100+ for real studies)   significant_count <- 0   for (sim in 1:50) {     # Simulate data     data1 <- simulate_lineup_data(n, n, d_prime = 1.8, lineup_size = 6, conf_levels = 5)     data2 <- simulate_lineup_data(n, n, d_prime = 1.5, lineup_size = 6, conf_levels = 5)      # Test     comp <- compare_pauc(data1, data2, n_bootstrap = 200, seed = sim)      if (comp$p_value < 0.05) {       significant_count <- significant_count + 1     }   }    power_results$power[i] <- significant_count / 50 }  # Display results cat("Power Analysis Results:
") print(power_results)  cat("
For 80% power, recommend n ≥", min(power_results$n[power_results$power >= 0.8]), "
")

title: SDT via GLM/GLMM
text: vignette shows estimate signal‑detection metrics old/new recognition data using GLM/GLMM methods, following approach described Wright, Horry, & Skagerberg (2009). Key idea: Encode item status (is_old) response (said_old) 0/1. Fit probit logit GLM/GLMM. coefficient is_old corresponds d′ (probit) lnOR (logit). centered coding (is_old → -0.5/+0.5), intercept corresponds criterion.

title: SDT via GLM/GLMM
code: library(r4lineups)  set.seed(123) n_subj <- 40 n_items <- 60 df <- data.frame(   subject_id = rep(1:n_subj, each = n_items),   item_id = rep(1:n_items, times = n_subj) ) df$is_old <- rbinom(nrow(df), 1, 0.5)  # true d' around 1.2 with mild subject variability subj_shift <- rnorm(n_subj, 0, 0.2) linpred <- (df$is_old * 1.2) + subj_shift[df$subject_id] df$said_old <- rbinom(nrow(df), 1, stats::pnorm(linpred))

title: SDT via GLM/GLMM

text: vignette demonstrates use r4lineups’ data simulation power analysis tools planning eyewitness identification studies. tools help researchers: Plan studies: Determine required sample sizes detecting effects Validate methods: Test analyses recover known parameters Explore scenarios: Compare different experimental designs Teach concepts: Demonstrate signal detection theory principles simulation framework implements equal-variance, independent-signal versions Independent Observations/MAX, Ensemble, Integration decision rules discussed Wixted et al. (2018). accepted "best_rest" option scale-equivalent parameterization Ensemble, fourth competing family.

title: Data Simulation and Power Analysis for Lineup Studies
text: simulation generates data using following SDT framework: Memory strength distributions: - Targets (guilty suspects): Normal(d’, 1) - Lures (foils/innocent suspects): Normal(0, 1) MAX decision rule: - witness selects lineup member highest memory strength - memory strengths criterion c, lineup rejected Parameters: - d_prime: Discriminability targets lures (higher = better memory) - c_criterion: Decision criterion (higher = conservative) - lineup_size: Number lineup members - conf_levels: Number confidence scale points lowest supplied c_criterion always identification-versus-rejection threshold. Additional strictly increasing criteria define confidence. scalar criterion retains value lowest threshold generates remaining confidence thresholds documented two-unit range; full control, supply one ordered criterion per confidence level.

title: Bayesian Calibration Analysis (Beta-Binomial Model) — calibration_bayes
text: confidence bin \(j\) \(n_j\) responses \(k_j\) correct identifications, posterior accuracy : $$a_j \mid \mathbf{n} \sim \mathrm{Beta}(k_j + \alpha,\; n_j - k_j + \alpha).$$ posterior draw \(s\), calibration statistics computed: $$C^{(s)} = \sum_j \frac{n_j}{N}(c_j - a_j^{(s)})^2$$ $$OU^{(s)} = \bar{c} - \sum_j \frac{n_j}{N} a_j^{(s)}$$ $$NRI^{(s)} = \frac{\sum_j \frac{n_j}{N}(a_j^{(s)} - \bar{}^{(s)})^2}{\bar{}^{(s)}(1-\bar{}^{(s)})}$$ \(c_j\) mean confidence (proportion scale) bin \(j\) \(\bar{c}\) overall mean confidence.

title: Bayesian Calibration Analysis (Beta-Binomial Model) — calibration_bayes
text: Juslin, P., Olsson, N., & Winman, . (1996). Calibration diagnosticity confidence eyewitness identification. Journal Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, Cognition, 22(5), 1304-1316. Brewer, N., & Wells, G. L. (2006). confidence-accuracy relationship eyewitness identification. Journal Experimental Psychology: Applied, 12(1), 11-30.

title: Bayesian Calibration Analysis (Beta-Binomial Model) — calibration_bayes
code: set.seed(42) n <- 200 conf  <- sample(c(50, 70, 90), n, replace = TRUE) tp    <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), n, replace = TRUE) ident <- ifelse(tp, "suspect", sample(c("suspect","filler","reject"), n, replace=TRUE)) df    <- data.frame(target_present = tp, identification = ident, confidence = conf) res   <- calibration_bayes(df, confidence_bins = c(0, 60, 80, 100)) print(res) #> Bayesian Calibration Analysis - Beta-Binomial model #>   n = 131; 3 confidence bins; prior alpha = 0.50 #>   C (calibration):      mean = 0.0266, median = 0.0255, 95% CI [0.0078, 0.0513] #>   O/U (over/underconf): mean = -0.1147, median = -0.1159, 95% CI [-0.1792, -0.0420] #>   NRI (resolution):     mean = 0.0327, median = 0.0274, 95% CI [0.0014, 0.0947] #>   (Frequentist: C = 0.0239, O/U = -0.1214, NRI = 0.0219) plot(res)

title: Compare pAUC Between Two ROC Curves — compare_pauc
text: function implements rigorous statistical test comparing ROC curves two conditions (e.g., simultaneous vs. sequential lineups, different retention intervals, etc.). **Method:** Computes pAUC condition (optionally maximum false ID rate) Uses bootstrap resampling estimate standard errors Computes Z-statistic: Z = (pAUC1 - pAUC2) / SE(pAUC1 - pAUC2) Calculates p-value standard normal distribution two datasets treated independent conditions. function implement paired clustered bootstrap. **Interpretation:** Positive pAUC difference: Condition 1 better discriminability Negative pAUC difference: Condition 2 better discriminability p < 0.05: Significant difference conditions

title: Compute ANRI (Adjusted Normalized Resolution Index) — compute_anri
text: ANRI corrects NRI small-sample small-bin-count bias: $$NRI = \frac{\frac{1}{N} \sum_{j=1}^{J} n_j (a_j - \bar{})^2}{\bar{}(1-\bar{})}$$ $$ANRI = \frac{N \cdot NRI - J + 1}{N - J + 1}$$ : N = total sample size J = number bins n_j = sample size bin j a_j = accuracy (proportion correct) bin j a_bar = overall accuracy **use ANRI vs NRI:** Use ANRI J small (e.g., 3-5 bins) Use ANRI N modest (e.g., < 200) Use ANRI comparing across different numbers bins NRI asymptotically unbiased N approaches infinity ANRI provides less biased estimate population resolution, making appropriate hypothesis testing group comparisons. target-absent suspect identifications estimated filler choices, N bin counts effective (possibly fractional) counts make_calibration_data(), correction approximation. See make_calibration_data designated-suspect distinction.

title: Compute Expected Information Gain (EIG) — compute_eig
text: EIG measures much information (bits) witness response provides guilt vs. innocence. computed : $$EIG = \sum_x p(x) \times [H(prior) - H(p(guilty|x))]$$ : x = response category (e.g., "suspect_high_confidence") p(x) = probability response H() = Shannon entropy p(guilty|x) = posterior probability guilt given response x Higher EIG values indicate diagnostic procedures. EIG = 0 means information gain (responses distinguish guilty innocent). EIG = 1 means perfect information (complete resolution uncertainty).

title: Compute Expected Information Gain (EIG) — compute_eig

title: Bayesian Diagnosticity Ratio (Tredoux, Beta-Binomial Model) — diag_ratio_T_bayes
text: lineup_pres numeric vector lineup choices target-present lineup. lineup_abs numeric vector lineup choices target-absent lineup. pos_pres Scalar; suspect position target-present lineup. pos_abs Scalar; suspect position target-absent lineup. k1 Number members target-present lineup (input validation). k2 Number members target-absent lineup (input validation). alpha Dirichlet concentration (prior strength). scalar \(\alpha > 0\) applied cells. Named shortcuts: "jeffreys" (0.5, default), "uniform" (1), "weak" (0.1). S Number posterior draws. Default 10000. credible_mass Width equal-tailed credible interval. Default 0.95. threshold Optional numeric. supplied, reports \(P(DR < t)\) \(P(DR > t | \mathbf{n})\).

title: Bayesian Diagnosticity Ratio (Tredoux, Beta-Binomial Model) — diag_ratio_T_bayes
text: object class "diag_ratio_T_bayes" containing: DR_draws Numeric vector length S: posterior draws DR. lnDR_draws Log-transformed posterior draws. posterior_mean, posterior_median Posterior point estimates. credible_interval Named two-element vector (lower, upper). prior_alpha Alpha value used. n_tp, n_ta, S, credible_mass Input metadata. threshold, threshold_probs Threshold associated probabilities (NULL).

title: Bayesian Diagnosticity Ratio (Tredoux, Beta-Binomial Model) — diag_ratio_T_bayes
text: target-present suspect-selection rate \(p_{TP}\) target-absent rate \(p_{TA}\) modelled independently Beta posteriors: $$p_{TP} \mid \mathbf{n} \sim \mathrm{Beta}(n_{TP,s} + \alpha,\; N_{TP} - n_{TP,s} + \alpha)$$ $$p_{TA} \mid \mathbf{n} \sim \mathrm{Beta}(n_{TA,s} + \alpha,\; N_{TA} - n_{TA,s} + \alpha)$$ posterior diagnosticity ratio obtained drawing \(DR^{(s)} = p_{TP}^{(s)} / p_{TA}^{(s)}\) sample \(s\). default Jeffreys prior (\(\alpha = 0.5\)) recommended small samples. Unlike continuity-corrected point estimate, posterior handles zero cell counts naturally provides direct probability statements \(P(DR > 1 \mid \mathbf{n})\).

title: Bayesian Posterior Distribution of Tredoux Effective Size — esize_T_bayes
text: Tredoux's effective size E' = 1/sum(p_i^2) mathematically identical   reciprocal Herfindahl-Hirschman concentration index   (Herfindahl, 1950; Hirschman, 1945) reciprocal   Simpson's (1949) concentration statistic lambda. Bayesian approach   estimates latent choice-probability vector p rather E' directly. mock-witness counts n = (n_1, ..., n_k) Dirichlet prior:   $$p \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_k),$$   posterior conjugate:   $$p \mid n \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(n_1 + \alpha_1, \ldots, n_k + \alpha_k).$$   posterior draw p mapped draw E' via E'(p) = 1/sum(p_i^2).   resulting posterior distribution E' summarises uncertainty   effective lineup size given observed choices. Dirichlet samples generated normalising independent Gamma draws   (base R ; additional package dependencies). publication, prior sensitivity analysis using least   alpha = 0.5, 1, 0.1 recommended. substantive conclusion   changes across priors, mock-witness sample likely small   support confident fairness conclusion.

University California Press. Simpson, E. H. (1949). Measurement diversity. Nature, 163, 688. Tredoux, C. G. (1998). Statistical inference measures lineup   fairness. Law Human Behavior, 22(2), 217-237.

text: restricted Independent Observations/MAX model simultaneous, fair lineups. Fillers IID \(N(0, 1)\), culprit signal \(N(d', 1)\), memory signals independent, single criterion applied largest signal. Target-absent n_fa therefore means choice lineup member, designated innocent suspect. lineup \(n\) members culprit signal strength \(d'\) response criterion \(\lambda\): $$P(\text{correct ID}) = \int_{\lambda}^{\infty} \phi(x - d') \Phi(x)^{n-1}\,dx$$ $$P(\text{choose anyone} \mid \text{TP}) = 1 - \Phi(\lambda - d')\Phi(\lambda)^{n-1}$$ $$P(\text{choose anyone} \mid \text{TA}) = 1 - \Phi(\lambda)^n$$ Parameters estimated minimizing Pearson chi-squared discrepancy mutually exclusive response cells: target-present correct ID, filler ID rejection; target-absent choice rejection. maximum-likelihood estimation multi-criterion likelihood model Wixted et al. (2018). Nested comparisons (equal d' equal lambda across conditions) supported via compare_max_sdt. Estimates conditional model assumptions. title: Fit Signal Detection Theory Model to ROC Data — fit_sdt_roc
text: **z-ROC Analysis**: z-ROC created plotting z-transformed hit rates z-transformed false alarm rates confidence level. equal-variance SDT: - z-ROC linear slope = 1 - d' = z(HR) - z(FAR) criterion - Intercept = d' line z(HR) = z(FAR) + d' unequal-variance SDT: - Slope = SD_lure / SD_target - Slope > 1 indicates greater variability lure distribution **Parameter Estimation**: - d' = average distance distributions standard deviation units - c = decision criterion (0 = unbiased, positive = conservative, negative = liberal) - Higher d' = better discriminability **Bootstrap Confidence Intervals**: bootstrap = TRUE, resamples data replacement estimate standard errors confidence intervals parameters.

title: Bayesian Functional Size (Beta-Binomial Model) — func_size_bayes
text: Functional size \(F = N / n_s\) reciprocal suspect-selection rate \(p = n_s / N\). Beta-Binomial conjugate model gives: $$p \mid \mathbf{n} \sim \mathrm{Beta}(n_s + \alpha,\; N - n_s + \alpha)$$ Posterior draws \(p^{(s)}\) transformed via \(F^{(s)} = 1/p^{(s)}\). default Jeffreys prior (\(\alpha = 0.5\)) recommended. posterior gives direct probability statements \(P(F < k \mid \mathbf{n})\), \(k\) nominal lineup size.

title: Bayesian Functional Size (Beta-Binomial Model) — func_size_bayes

title: Bayesian Functional Size (Beta-Binomial Model) — func_size_bayes
code: set.seed(1) lineup_vec <- round(runif(100, 1, 6)) res <- func_size_bayes(lineup_vec, target_pos = 3) print(res) #> Bayesian Functional Size - Beta-Binomial model #>   Prior: Jeffreys-type Beta(0.50, 0.50) #>   n = 100, suspect IDs = 28 (rate = 0.280) #>   Posterior mean F:   3.637 #>   Posterior median F: 3.567 #>   95% credible interval: [2.673, 5.034] plot(res)   # Threshold: P(F < 6 | data) res_t <- func_size_bayes(lineup_vec, target_pos = 3, threshold = 6) print(res_t) #> Bayesian Functional Size - Beta-Binomial model #>   Prior: Jeffreys-type Beta(0.50, 0.50) #>   n = 100, suspect IDs = 28 (rate = 0.280) #>   Posterior mean F:   3.637 #>   Posterior median F: 3.563 #>   95% credible interval: [2.668, 5.005] #>   P(F < 6.000 | data): 0.9983 #>   P(F > 6.000 | data): 0.0017

title: I Component of Tredoux Effective Size (Tredoux, 1998) — i_esize_T

title: Compute Bayesian Prior-Posterior and Information Gain Curves — make_bayes_curves
text: function treats lineup outcomes evidence Bayesian updating. response type x (e.g., high-confidence suspect ID, rejection, etc.), computes: Likelihoods observed data: $$p(x|guilty) = \frac{count(x | target\_present)}{N_{guilty}}$$ $$p(x|innocent) = \frac{count(x | target\_absent)}{N_{innocent}}$$ prior probability p(guilty): $$p(x) = p(guilty) \cdot p(x|guilty) + (1-p(guilty)) \cdot p(x|innocent)$$ $$p(guilty|x) = \frac{p(guilty) \cdot p(x|guilty)}{p(x)}$$ Information gain: $$IG(x) = H(prior) - H(posterior)$$ H(p) binary entropy. information gain quantifies much uncertainty reduced observing response x. Positive values indicate response diagnostic.

title: Compute Bayesian Prior-Posterior and Information Gain Curves — make_bayes_curves

title: Compute Calibration Statistics for Eyewitness Identification — make_calibration_data
text: Calibration analysis distinguishes : Calibration (C): well confidence matches accuracy (perfect = 0) /underconfidence (O/U): Overall bias confidence judgments (0 = perfectly calibrated) Resolution (NRI): Ability discriminate correct incorrect responses calibration statistic C measures weighted mean squared deviation mean confidence accuracy bin: $$C = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \frac{n_j}{N} (c_j - a_j)^2$$ Normalized Resolution Index (NRI) captures well confidence discriminates correct incorrect responses: $$NRI = \frac{\frac{1}{N} \sum_{j=1}^{J} n_j (a_j - \bar{})^2}{\bar{}(1-\bar{})}$$ choosers_only = TRUE, suspect identifications included (standard eyewitness calibration analysis). choosers_only = FALSE, responses included fillers rejections counted incorrect. target-absent data contain designated innocent-suspect identifications, observations used directly. Otherwise, target-absent filler identification contributes weight 1 / lineup_size estimate innocent-suspect identifications. latter case per-bin counts effective total used C, O/U, NRI, downstream ANRI can fractional; results lineup-size approximations rather statistics observed designated-suspect outcome.

title: Compute Deviation from Perfect Performance (DPP) — make_dpp
text: DPP (Deviation Perfect Performance) compares observed ROC curve perfect ROC curve within false alarm rate range: $$DPP = 1 - \frac{AUC_{observed}}{AUC_{perfect}}$$ : Perfect ROC: Goes (0,0) → (0,1) → (max_FA,1)     (immediate jump 100 Observed ROC: Actual performance data AUC: Area curve computed via trapezoidal rule **Interpretation**: DPP = 0: Perfect performance (correct IDs 0 DPP → 1: poor performance (near chance) Lower DPP = better performance **Advantages pAUC** (Smith et al. 2018): Less affected ROC truncation (different confidence distributions) Normalized relative best achievable performance consistent rankings across datasets Accounts achievable performance given observed FA range perfect ROC constrained FA range observed data, making DPP fair measure even procedures produce different confidence distributions (thus different ROC truncation points).

title: Compute Full ROC Data for Lineup Identification (Smith & Yang, 2020) — make_fullroc_data
text: function implements "full ROC" method described Smith & Yang (2020). Unlike traditional partial ROC curves use suspect identifications, method uses eyewitness responses: Suspect identifications (evidence guilt) Filler identifications (evidence innocence) Lineup rejections (evidence innocence) response type crossed confidence levels create decision criteria. ordered diagnosticity ratio (HR/FAR) -priori ordering, cumulative hit false alarm rates computed form full ROC curve. full ROC provides threshold-free measure investigator discriminability— ability distinguish guilty innocent suspects using available eyewitness evidence. Note ordering bias: ordering cells sample diagnosticity ratio (order = "diagnosticity") bows curve upward noise alone, resulting AUC optimistically biased — identical target-present target-absent response distributions yield AUC slightly 0.5, bias growing number decision--confidence cells shrinking sample size. inference comparisons across conditions, prefer order = "apriori" (theoretically fixed ordering suggested Smith & Yang, 2020) compare permutation baseline.

Default = 0.5. utility_matrix Named numeric vector utilities/costs : tp: True positive (correct suspect ID) - typically positive fn: False negative (miss/rejection guilty) - typically negative fp: False positive (innocent suspect ID) - typically negative tn: True negative (correct rejection innocent) - typically positive Default: c(tp=1, fn=-0.5, fp=-2, tn=0.5) lineup_size Integer. title: Compute Expected Utility Curves for Lineup Identification — make_utility_curves
text: Expected utility combines hit rates false alarm rates costs/benefits different outcomes: $$EU = base\_rate \cdot [hit \cdot U_{TP} + (1-hit) \cdot U_{FN}] +$$ $$     (1-base\_rate) \cdot [fa \cdot U_{FP} + (1-fa) \cdot U_{TN}]$$ : hit = p(suspect ID | guilty) criterion fa = p(suspect ID | innocent) criterion U_TP, U_FN, U_FP, U_TN = utilities outcome utility matrix reflect relative value/cost outcomes. example: tp = 1: Correctly identifying perpetrator fn = -0.5: Missing perpetrator (remain large) fp = -2: Wrongly convicting innocent person (severe injustice) tn = 0.5: Correctly rejecting innocent Lampinen et al. (2019) show comparing procedures ROC curves alone can misleading. Utility analysis incorporates base rates relative costs errors, providing complete evaluation. Note false-alarm estimate: explicit target-absent suspect IDs used present. Otherwise, filler IDs divided lineup size. Direct filler-derived estimates never added together.

text: Utility difference curves show relative value two procedures changes base rate (prevalence) guilty suspects. addresses question: "procedure better, depend base rate?" $$Utility Difference = EU_A - EU_B$$ Interpretation: Positive difference: Procedure higher utility (preferred) Negative difference: Procedure B higher utility (preferred) Zero difference: Procedures equivalent base rate Lampinen et al. (2019) show ROC dominance guarantee utility dominance. procedure lower pAUC might higher utility certain base rates cost structures.

title: Compute Utility Difference Curves Comparing Two Procedures — make_utility_difference
text: Lampinen, J. M., Smith, . M., & Wells, G. L. (2019). Four utilities eyewitness identification practice: Dissociations receiver operating characteristic analysis expected utility analysis. Law Human Behavior, 43(1), 26-44.

title: Compute PPV by Confidence with Lineup Size Correction — ppv_by_confidence
text: data dataframe columns: target_present: Logical. TRUE guilty suspect lineup identification: Character. "suspect", "filler", "reject" confidence: Numeric. Confidence rating lineup_size Integer. Nominal number people lineup (default = 6) confidence_bins Numeric vector bin edges grouping confidence (e.g., c(0, 60, 80, 100)). NULL, uses individual confidence levels. correction Character. Method estimating innocent-suspect IDs: "nominal" (best-case, assumes fair lineup), "effective" (accounts bias), "none" (worst-case, correction). Default = "nominal". effective_size_data Optional dataframe pre-computed effective sizes per confidence bin (must columns: conf_level, effective_size). NULL correction="effective", computes data.

title: Compute PPV by Confidence with Lineup Size Correction — ppv_by_confidence
text: list containing: ppv_data: Dataframe PPV confidence level overall_ppv: Overall PPV across confidence levels correction_method: correction method used lineup_size: Nominal lineup size

title: Compute PPV by Confidence with Lineup Size Correction — ppv_by_confidence
text: PPV (Positive Predictive Value) probability suspect guilty given identification. formula : PPV = guilty_suspect_IDs / (guilty_suspect_IDs + innocent_suspect_IDs) Different correction methods estimate innocent_suspect_IDs differently: "nominal": assumes perfect lineup fairness (error_rate / lineup_size) "effective": uses effective size account bias (error_rate / effective_size) "none": assumes errors innocent-suspect IDs (error_rate) Note implicit base rate: PPV computed raw target-present target-absent counts, prior probability guilt implicitly experiment's TP:TA ratio (e.g., 0.5 usual balanced design). PPV base-rate-free: different real-world base rates PPV procedure differ. target-absent lineups designated innocent suspect, correction also relies pseudo-distribution assumption spreading filler choices lineup members, modeling approximation.

title: Compute PPV by Confidence with Lineup Size Correction — ppv_by_confidence
text: Fitzgerald, R. J., Tredoux, C. G., & Juncu, S. (2023). Estimation eyewitness error rates fair biased lineups. Law Human Behavior.

title: Bayesian Comparison of SDT Sensitivity (d') Between Two Conditions — sdt_compare
text: Independent Jeffreys Beta posteriors placed hit false-alarm rates condition: $$HR_A \mid \mathbf{n} \sim \mathrm{Beta}(\text{hits}_A + \alpha,\; \text{misses}_A + \alpha)$$ $$FAR_A \mid \mathbf{n} \sim \mathrm{Beta}(\text{fas}_A + \alpha,\; \text{crs}_A + \alpha)$$ posterior d' draws : $$d'^{(s)}_A = \Phi^{-1}(HR_A^{(s)}) - \Phi^{-1}(FAR_A^{(s)})$$ analogously B. posterior difference \(\Delta d'^{(s)} = d'^{(s)}_A - d'^{(s)}_B\), \(P(d'_A > d'_B \mid \mathbf{n})\) directly read . Jeffreys prior (\(\alpha = 0.5\)) handles zero cell counts gracefully provides direct probability statements - unlike asymptotic z-test compare_sdt_summary.
